title: Invoice Index By ID
prompt: A C# repository layer wants dictionary-style lookup for invoices. Write a function that returns an object keyed by id, with the full item as the value.

explanation.beginner:
Example: invoiceIndexById([{"id":"a","number":"Alpha"},{"id":"b","number":"Beta"}]) produces {"a":{"id":"a","number":"Alpha"},"b":{"id":"b","number":"Beta"}}. Associate each record with its stable ID. Each assignment updates one lookup entry; duplicate IDs follow the stated overwrite rule.

Compare “handles empty lists”: input [[]] produces {}. Explain which rule causes the difference before writing code.
explanation.junior:
Associate each record with its stable ID. Each assignment updates one lookup entry; duplicate IDs follow the stated overwrite rule.

Tempting mistake: Array positions are not stable identifiers after sorting or filtering. Repeated IDs require an explicit first-wins or last-wins policy.

Trace the branch conditions and any accumulator or lookup after each input. Keep the return contract separate from how it is calculated.

Regression check: preserve the contract illustrated by “handles empty lists”, then change one boundary in a new test. The solution below is one implementation; another is valid when it preserves the same behavior.
